# Fairstay Managed Care Claims (`fairstay-managed-care-claims`)

Checks nursing-home managed care claims (HMO, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid MCO) against contract per-diem rates and authorizations: no contract rate, billed below contract, paid below contract, missing or unknown authorization numbers, levels not authorized and days outside the authorization. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Managed Care Claims never submits claims or appeals. Fairstay Managed Care Claims never logs in to plan portals.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Managed care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-managed-care-claims demo
npx -y fairstay-managed-care-claims mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional managed care plans and residents, March 2026. Planted: M7002 paid 1,550 under contract, M7003 billed level L3 on an L2 authorization that ended 14 March, M7004 billed 675 below the contract rate, M7005 no authorization number, M7006 an authorization number not in the log, M7007 a level with no contract rate. M7001 is clean.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `mcclaims_check` | List managed care claim problems: authorization first, then rates. | runs |
| `mcclaims_write_report` | Write mcclaims-managed-care.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and mcclaims-managed-care.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/mcclaims). | runs |
| `mcclaims_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `mcclaims_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `mcclaims_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `mcclaims_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Fairstay Managed Care Claims never submits claims or appeals. | refused |
| `payer_portal_login` | Fairstay Managed Care Claims never logs in to plan portals. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `mcclaims_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `claims` (required) | Managed care claims under --root: claim, resident, payer, level, from, through, days, billed, paid, authorization number |
| `rates` (required) | Contract rates under --root (CSV or Excel): payer, level, per-diem rate, effective from and to |
| `auths` (required) | Authorization log under --root: authorization number, resident, payer, level, from, to |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-managed-care-claims inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Managed care claims (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` (required) | text | Claim, Claim ID, Claim #, Invoice # |
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Service From, Statement From |
| `through` | date | Through, Thru, Service To, Statement Thru |
| `days` | number | Days, Units, Covered Days |
| `billed` | amount | Billed, Charges, Billed Amount, Total Charges |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Paid Amount, Payment, Allowed Paid |
| `auth_number` | text | Auth Number, Authorization Number, Auth #, Prior Auth, Reference Number, Auth |

### Contract rates (`rates`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `level` (required) | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `rate` (required) | amount | Rate, Per Diem, Daily Rate, Contract Rate |
| `from` | date | From, Effective, Effective Date, Start |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Term Date |

### Authorization log (`auths`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `auth_number` (required) | text | Auth Number, Authorization Number, Auth #, Prior Auth, Reference Number, Auth |
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `from` | date | From, Start Date, Auth From, Effective Date |
| `to` | date | To, End Date, Auth To, Expiration Date |

## Memory

`mcclaims_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `mcclaims_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `level_alias` | reads the code as that level for that payer. It changes how levels are read, never a rate. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-managed-care-claims": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-managed-care-claims",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-managed-care-claims -- npx -y fairstay-managed-care-claims mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-managed-care-claims tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-managed-care-claims sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-managed-care-claims inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-managed-care-claims call mcclaims_check '{"claims":"<claims>","rates":"<rates>","auths":"<auths>"}'
fairstay-managed-care-claims eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-managed-care-claims demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
